page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.32-128 is an ARM64 virtual compute instance utilizing Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running 64 vCPUs at a single thread per core, eliminating performance contention common in simultaneous multithreading (SMT) environments. The instance is paired with 128.0 GB of system RAM, providing an exact memory density of 2.0 GB per core, aligning with compute-focused sizing profiles.

The instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, requiring persistence and high-throughput disk operations to be mounted via remote block storage services. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned for direct network routing. From an efficiency standpoint, the dedicated physical ARM core model offers predictable instruction throughput and sustained compute density across all 64 cores without virtualization-level thread sharing overhead.

This hardware balance makes the instance suited for compute-intensive and highly threaded applications that run natively on 64-bit ARM architectures. Prime deployment scenarios include distributed web serving, containerized microservices orchestration, continuous integration and build pipelines, and parallel data transformation tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.32-128 is an ARM64 compute-oriented virtual machine powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores running 64 vCPUs with a strict one-thread-per-core configuration, avoiding resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading. It includes 128.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without local storage or discrete GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for persistent file systems, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Due to its dedicated physical core layout, this server offers predictable multi-core throughput and high core density relative to resource usage. It is well suited for horizontally scaled cloud-native microservices, software compilation clusters, continuous integration build jobs, and scalable web serving.
